author: Michael Starkie
why: Camera photograph of an open-mouthed common hippo in Tanzania, identified in the caption and safari tags. Strong mouth-and-teeth emphasis; not a whole-body land view.

author: Marijn van der Marel
why: Large standing common hippo photographed in Nyerere National Park, Tanzania. Strong land-based candidate with a clearly documented wild location; native dimensions unverified.

author: Bob Brewer
why: Yawning common hippo photographed in Ruaha National Park, Tanzania. Open-mouth alternative with strong facial impact; body partly submerged.

author: Hugo Sykes
why: Alternative land photograph of a wild common hippo in Kenyan savanna. Open surroundings offer cropping flexibility; sex and native dimensions unverified.

author: Adriaan Greyling
why: 6609 × 4409 photograph of a hippo grazing beside a river, with birds and lush vegetation. Environmental alternative; animal prominence after a 9:10 crop needs checking.

author: Alex Kraft
why: Wild common hippo grazing in Murchison Falls National Park, Uganda. Broad body visible against lush vegetation; grass partly obscures the feet.

author: Linda
why: Lakeshore grazing hippo photographed in Tanzania's Arusha Region. Source lists a 4912 × 3264 camera photograph; useful full-body habitat option.

author: Colin Watts
why: Common hippo family at a lakeshore in South Africa, identified by the photographer. Standing animals provide more body visibility; group composition needs a selective crop.

author: Hugo Sykes
why: Common hippopotamus grazing on land in Narok, Kenya; strong habitat and body-view candidate. Mouth closed; native dimensions and exact 9:10 crop unverified.

author: Jonathan Göhner
why: Captioned warning display, with Uganda and River Nile location tags. Large open jaws and visible tusks suit a tight 9:10 card; lower body submerged.

author: Charlie Summers
why: Caption explicitly identifies a Hippopotamus amphibius bull charging into the South Luangwa River, Zambia. Excellent male/action match; linked 1024px size is below the preferred resolution.
